references.text: The same ritual of smearing blood on the horns of the altar and pouring out the rest of the blood at the base of the burnt offering altar, here performed for a priest who has sinned.
An identical blood ritual for the sin offering when the whole congregation of Israel has sinned—the blood is smeared on the horns of the altar and the remainder is poured out at its base.

A parallel text concerning a sin offering for a leader: the priest takes some blood with his finger, smears it on the horns of the burnt offering altar, and pours out the rest at the foot of the altar.
The same blood ritual repeated for a sin offering involving a lamb—blood on the horns and the remainder poured out at the base of the altar.
Moses performs this ritual during the consecration of Aaron and his sons—blood on the horns of the altar and the rest poured out at its base.
Aaron's sons bring the blood to him, he dips his finger into it, smears it on the horns of the altar, and pours out the remainder at the foot of the altar.
Instructions for the burnt offering altar: the blood is to be smeared on the horns of the altar with the finger, and the rest poured out at its base.

The Letter to the Hebrews explains that under the law almost everything is cleansed with blood, and without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness—this is the theological foundation for the blood rituals in Leviticus.
